transcript: Okay, fine. I'm going to weigh in on the Eddie Redmayne MC discourse because some people seem to really like him, some people seem to not really like him. And honestly, I think everyone's a little bit wrong, because on one side, you have the people that don't like his performance that say it's just too creepy and off putting and he's doing too much. And then on the other side, you have the people that do like his performance that are saying, yes, but the MC is supposed to be creepy and off putting. So you just. You just don't get it. And while I fully agree that the MC should be creepy and off putting, I don't think he should be creepy and off putting. The opening number. I mentioned this in my full cabaret review, but I think the best productions of cabaret are the ones that are able to lure you in and then pull the rug out from under you. That's important because it implicates the audience and shows you how easy it is to get swept up by charismatic leaders if you are not careful, if you are not discerning. That's my main problem with Eddie's MC, is I didn't find him charismatic because he is so immediately off putting. You immediately understand what his deal is and to be wary of him. And so personally, I did not find it as effective as past versions of the character have been. But if you Are one of the people that liked Eddie's MC. That's fine. You're allowed to like it. What has been so frustrating about this discourse is on both sides. People claiming you just don't get the show, like I get the show. Because art is subjective, and it is going to mean different things and resonate differently with different people. And so we can engage with it critically. We can debate back and forth about why Eddie's MC did or didn't work for us. Don't shut down someone else's opinion because it doesn't align with yours. And don't tell them they just didn't get it. Because in my opinion, not only is it not productive, but it is actively anti art.
